description: Why test, testing in the SDLC

screens.body:
Every app has bugs — including yours, including mine. Testing is how you find them before your users do.

The earlier you catch a bug, the cheaper it is to fix. A bug found while you're writing the code takes minutes. The same bug found after launch can cost money, users, and sleep.

options: Bugs are cheaper to fix early
Testing is only for big companies
check.question: Why test early in the process?

screens.heading: Why test at all?
screens.keyPoint: Testing finds bugs before users do — earlier is cheaper.

screens.body:
Testing and debugging are partners, not the same job. Testing asks: "does this work?" Debugging asks: "why doesn't this work?"

You test first to find the problem. Then you debug to fix it. Then you test again to make sure the fix worked — and didn't break anything else.
screens.heading: Testing vs debugging
screens.keyPoint: Testing finds problems; debugging fixes them.

screens.body:
SDLC stands for Software Development Life Cycle: plan, design, build, test, deploy, maintain.

Testing isn't just one phase at the end — it runs alongside development. You write code, you test it, you fix it, you ship it. Good teams test continuously, not once at the finish line.
screens.heading: Testing in the SDLC
screens.keyPoint: Testing runs through the whole SDLC, not just at the end.

screens.body:
Not all tests are equal. The test pyramid says: write LOTS of small, fast unit tests at the bottom. Fewer integration tests in the middle. A handful of slow end-to-end tests at the top.

The pyramid keeps you fast: most bugs get caught by the cheap tests at the bottom, long before the slow tests at the top run.

check.question: The base of the test pyramid is…

screens.heading: The test pyramid
screens.keyPoint: Many fast unit tests, few slow end-to-end tests.

screens.body:
Manual testing means a human clicks through the app, trying things. Automated testing means scripts do the clicking for you.

Manual is great for exploring and for "does this feel right?" Automated is great for repeating the same checks every single day without getting bored. Use both.

options: Judging whether a design feels nice
check.question: Automated tests are best for…

screens.heading: Manual vs automated

screens.body:
Almost every test follows three steps: Arrange, Act, Assert. Set up the situation, do the thing, check the result.

For example: arrange — create a cart with 2 items. Act — apply a 10% discount. Assert — the total should be 90% of the original. That rhythm is the whole game.

options: Check the result is what you expected
check.question: In Arrange-Act-Assert, 'Assert' means…

screens.heading: Anatomy of a test
screens.keyPoint: Arrange, Act, Assert — the rhythm of every test.

screens.body:
Think about SwiftGigs: escrow holds real money between strangers. If the release-payment logic has a bug, someone loses actual cash.

Testing isn't homework — it's how you protect your users and your reputation. The escrow dApp you built for that job demo? The first thing a serious reviewer would ask is: "where are the tests?"

options: Real money moves through that code
check.question: For SwiftGigs escrow, testing matters because…

screens.heading: Why this matters for you
screens.keyPoint: Tests protect real money and real users.
